lines.li: [them,their:tribal] At the fires they say your healers send the sick home on their feet.
[them,their:medieval] In the market they say your {HOSPITAL} sends folk home on their feet.
[them,their:hightech] People on the road say your {HOSPITAL} is worth the walk.
[them] People on the road speak well of your {HOSPITAL}.
[us,colony:doctor] That's {DOCTOR}'s doing, mostly.
[us] We do what we can for whoever comes.
[them] That counts for a lot out here.
[them] Your {HOSPITAL} is known across the whole region now.
[us] So we keep hearing.
[them,their:empire] Word of it has reached even our people, who listen to very little.
[them,their:tribal] The sick will walk many sleeps for hands they can trust.
[them] The sick will come a long way for a doctor they can trust.
[us,colony:doctor] Then {DOCTOR} had better get some sleep while there's time.
[us] Then we'd best keep the beds clean and the door open.
[them] Is {DOCTOR} the doctor people talk about?
[us] That's {DOCTOR}, who has pulled more than a few of us through.
[them,their:tribal] Then the spirits guide those hands.
[them,their:medieval] Then I'll remember the name, should I ever need it.
[them] Good to know, should I ever need one.
[us,their:tribal] I'll tell {DOCTOR} you said so.
[us] Let's hope you never do.
[them] You're the doctor they talk about on the road, aren't you?
[us,trait:Kind] I suppose I am, though I only do what anyone would.
[us] I suppose I am, though I'd rather they talked about the weather.
[them,their:medieval] Our reeve would pay good silver for hands like yours.
[them,their:tribal] Our healer would sit at your feet to learn, I think.
[them] Then I'll know whose door to knock on.
[us,their:medieval] Silver's welcome, but I'd sooner nobody needed me.
[us,their:tribal] Then we'd have a lot to talk about.
[us] Knock, and I'll see what I can do.
[them] With {ILL} ill at home, I wish we had a {HOSPITAL} like yours.
[us,lowtech] It's only clean linen, a warm fire and someone who knows what to do.
[us] It's only clean beds and a doctor who knows what to do.
[them,their:tribal] Then our elders should hear how it is done here.
[them,their:empire] Then I shall describe it to our physicians, who will not listen.
[them] Then I'll tell them at home how you go about it.
[them] A {HOSPITAL} with a name like yours must go through a lot of medicine.
[us] It does, so we're always glad of a trader.
[them,their:hightech] Then you'll want a look at my goods before I pack up.
[them] Then have a look at my goods before I go.
[them] Is it true your {HOSPITAL} makes sick people better?
[us,us:doctor] Most of the time, and I'm the one who does it.
[us] Most of the time, yes.
[them] I'm going to be a doctor when I'm big, then.
[them] Your {HOSPITAL} has quite a name, I hear.
[us] It earned it one patient at a time.
